title: Type I and Type X
coreMove: Shift behavior toward Type I by supporting autonomy, competence, and relatedness instead of relying on external pressure alone.

exampleSpecs.audience: Harper, a manager redesigning a performance conversation
exampleSpecs.stakes: A review cycle may label employees before examining the conditions around them.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Type I and Type X as patterns shaped by environment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Quentin, an adviser helping a graduate student regain agency
exampleSpecs.stakes: A student is doing the minimum after months of vague criticism.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use autonomy, competence, and relatedness as repair handles.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bianca, a founder separating drive from status hunger
exampleSpecs.stakes: A hiring panel is mistaking intensity for internal motivation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the difference between Type I drive and Type X pressure.

exampleSpecs.audience: Darius, a conservatory coach reframing struggle
exampleSpecs.stakes: A musician reads a difficult passage as proof of lacking talent.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use competence support without pretending the struggle is easy.

exampleSpecs.audience: Iris, a sales director replacing pressure with need support
exampleSpecs.stakes: A regional reset is pushing numbers up but burning people down.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Type X pressure being redesigned toward Type I conditions.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rafael, a family-business successor naming an inherited reward habit
exampleSpecs.stakes: A retreat has to separate family approval from good business judgment.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Type X behavior as trained, not innate.
